chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu Maryam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Al-Mut'ah: the Quran was revealed concerning it, and the Sunnah from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) flowed by it.
ai.seo_question: What is the Quranic and Prophetic evidence for Mut'ah in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this foundational hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) explicitly links the institution of Mut'ah to both the Quranic revelation and the Prophetic Sunnah, establishing it as a divinely sanctioned practice rather than a later juristic innovation. This narration is pivotal in Shia fiqh for affirming the validity of temporary marriage, particularly in contexts of travel or necessity, and underscores its continuity until the time of Umar ibn al-Khattab. The emphasis on 'Sunnah' here refers to the established practice of the Prophet, reinforcing the dual-source authority of Quran and Hadith in Shia legal theory.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban Bin Usman, from Abu Maryam, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The Mut’a - the Quran came down with it, and the Sunnah from Rasool-Allahsaww flowed by it’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from abu Maryam who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

Al-Mut‘ah (advantageous marriage) is mentioned in al- Quran and the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has followed it.’”
